source_refs.note: Topic 11.2.3 (Nomenclature of cycloalkanes) with Figure 11.3 and Quick Check 11.1, printed page 249.

blocks.text: Cycloalkanes are named by attaching the prefix ‘cyclo’ to the names of the alkanes possessing the same number of carbon atoms. Figure 11.3

blocks.alt: In one row, as printed: Four cyclohexane rings with side chains in condensed form. Ethylcyclohexane: CH2-CH3 on the ring. Isopropylcyclohexane: H3C-CH-CH3 with chain numbers 1 and 2; common name isopropylcyclohexane, IUPAC name 1-methylethylcyclohexane. 1,1,4-Trimethylcyclohexane: ring numbered 1 to 4, CH3 on carbon 4 and H3C and CH3 on carbon 1. n-Propylcyclohexane: CH2-CH2-CH3; IUPAC name propylcyclohexane.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.3: Naming cycloalkanes (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.3).

blocks.prompt: a) Write down the structural formulas for 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.
blocks.explanation:
2-Methylbutane: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₃, a four-carbon chain with a methyl group on carbon 2.
2,2-Dimethylpropane: C(CH₃)₄, a three-carbon chain with two methyl groups on carbon 2.
Both are C₅H₁₂.

blocks.prompt: b) Write down displayed formula of 2,3,3-trimethylhexane and methylcyclohexane.
blocks.explanation:
2,3,3-Trimethylhexane: a six-carbon chain with one methyl group on carbon 2 and two on carbon 3: CH₃CH(CH₃)C(CH₃)₂CH₂CH₂CH₃.
Methylcyclohexane: a six-carbon ring with a CH₃ group on one carbon, C₇H₁₄.

blocks.prompt: c) Give two differences between molecules of cyclopentane and pentane?
blocks.explanation: Cyclopentane (C₅H₁₀) has its five carbon atoms in a ring and two hydrogen atoms fewer than pentane (C₅H₁₂). The carbon atoms of pentane form an open chain with two CH₃ ends; the ring has no ends.

rows: five carbon atoms in a ring (cyclic)
five carbon atoms in an open chain
two CH₃ ends and three CH₂ groups

blocks.prompt: d) Eicosane is a straight chain alkane whose molecules contain 20 carbon atoms. What is the molecular formula of eicosane?
